ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle B=60^\circ$, and the diagonal $AC=10$. What is the perimeter and the area of the rhombus?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line BD intersecting AC at O, as shown in the figure:\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus,\\
$\therefore$ AB=AC, $AC\perp BD$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ABC=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ AC=AB=10, AO=5,\\
By Pythagoras' theorem, BO=$5\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ The perimeter of the rhombus is $4\times 10=\boxed{40}$, the area of the rhombus is $2AO\times BO=10\times 5\sqrt{3}=\boxed{50\sqrt{3}}$.
